titleEn: If You Lose Us, Stay Right There!

pages.text: "Everyone hold my apron!" Grandpa Badger held its edge behind him. Each friend gripped it with one hand. The winter market was crowded.
"I want dried fruit!" Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, stretched the neck toward a pile of red dried fruit. Gugu quietly let go and slipped into the crowd.
Looking back, Gugu could not see the apron, Grandpa, Nono, or Kiki. Gugu's beak trembled.
Gugu held back tears, remembering Grandpa's words. "If you lose us, stay right there!" Instead of running, Gugu stopped both feet and took a deep breath.
Gugu raised the green bag overhead. In the gray market, it was the only green bag. "Grandpa! Gugu is here!" came a loud call.
Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, saw green beyond the crowd. "There!" All three hurried over. Grandpa lifted Gugu into a snug hug.
"You stayed put instead of running. Well done." Gugu held the apron again. "If you lose us, stay right there!"
Gugu touched the green bag strap. "We could see it from far away!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, smiled. The four walked together, holding the apron.
Now Gugu was not afraid in the market. "One, stay right there! Two, lift the green bag and call loudly! Three, tell a grown-up at a shop and wait!" Leaving, Gugu held the apron tightest.

Back at the shop, Nono and Kiki buried their faces against Gugu's shoulders. Stop instead of running when lost, and you can meet again soon. Gugu raised both hands. "If you lose us, stay right there!"
